claims.statement: buildCoachCheckInReport() in src/lib/coach-check-in.ts is a pure function: given sessions, working sets, program days/slots/phases, the exercise catalog, and bodyweight context, it returns only facts and classifications, never programming recommendations, and never mutates training data.

The CoachCheckInReport uses America/Chicago as the default reporting timezone; the current window is the seven calendar dates ending on generatedAt, the prior window is the immediately preceding seven dates, the two never overlap, sessions are windowed by performed_at excluding future sessions, and only sessions with finished_at contribute to execution metrics (open sessions become a data-quality warning).

Duration, set-execution, RIR-execution, and hard-set/specialization metrics in CoachWindowReport are computed against the historical session's stored week_index (so deload set multipliers and RIR ranges apply to that exposure), with duration excluded/flagged outside 5-240 minutes, and each specialization group additionally reports prescribedSets (schema-1.0-additive) skipping prescriptions whose target RIR floor is above 1.

Exercise trend classification requires four completed exposures with valid e1RM values; gaining/declining requires both of the last two exposures to clear both of the preceding two by a 1% noise margin, otherwise the classification is flat, and fewer than four valid exposures yields insufficient_data.

CoachCheckInReport never includes email addresses, auth claims, user IDs, session IDs, program IDs, program-day IDs, or program-slot IDs, and consumers are expected to key on the version field before relying on its shape; the report re-resolves the current slot definition against the session's stored week rather than snapshotting the prescription at workout start.

buildCoachRecommendations() in src/lib/coach-recommendations.ts is a deterministic layer, kept separate from coach-check-in.ts, that consumes the canonical report plus the same raw rows, delegates normal overload to sessionTarget(), and never mutates a program, slot, set, or session.

Per active-program slot, recommendationForSlot() applies a fixed guardrail order: significant joint pain in the current window suppresses all slots and returns a single pain_review recommendation first; then an effective deload phase (via resolvePrescription()+isDeload()) returns deload_hold; then two consecutive harder-than-target first sets return an effort-based reduce_load; then a stall-report plateau whose latest stalled point matches the latest exposure returns plateau_review; then one down exposure (>1% below only the immediately preceding exposure) returns keep_movement instead of a plateau/swap call; only then does normal sessionTarget() double progression apply; a slot with no finished linked exposure returns insufficient_data instead of a cross-exercise estimate.

sessionTarget()-based progression in the recommendations engine anchors on the slot's latest exact-exercise exposure via selectProgressionReference()/exerciseProgressionReference(), so a stronger first set on another program day after that anchor can advance the target but an older all-time best cannot; a first set below rep_min yields a rep-floor target with load recalibrated from observed reps/RIR, and generated targets never prescribe reps outside the slot's range.

Every CoachRecommendation carries an opaque key computed by stableKey() from kind, slotId, exerciseId, latest evidence timestamp, action, target weight/reps, and summary, so a new exposure produces a new key; recommendations also carry program-day context, action, rationale, evidence window/count/summary, confidence, dataSufficiency text, and priority.

rankCoachRecommendations() scores each recommendation as CONFIDENCE_SCORE[confidence] times kindImpact(kind, isCompound), assigns priority "now" to pain_review or any score at/above NOW_SCORE (16, e.g. medium-or-better add_load on a compound), otherwise "next", and sorts by score descending with slot order as a stable tiebreak; formatCoachRecommendations() and the UI render mixed lists as Do first / Also tiers, and double progression is never reinvented by ranking.

Accept, dismiss, and defer decisions write only to coach_recommendation_decision; pendingCoachRecommendations() filters out insufficient_data/insufficient confidence, accepted/dismissed items, and deferred items whose deferredUntil has not passed, so a deferred proposal stays hidden for 7 days while a new exposure's new key produces a fresh, undismissed proposal; the API and clipboard export retain the full diagnostic set regardless of review-state filtering in the UI.

createCoachWeeklyHandler() in src/lib/coach-api.ts fails closed with 503 when COACH_API_TOKEN is missing/under 32 chars or COACH_API_USER_ID is missing/not UUID-shaped, before any credential check; a missing or mismatched token (checked via constant-time SHA-256 digest comparison, supporting both an Authorization Bearer header and a ?token= capability-URL fallback that cannot be overridden by an invalid header) returns an identical generic 401 in both cases.

The weekly Coach API always sets Cache-Control private/no-store/max-age=0, Pragma no-cache, Vary Authorization, and X-Robots-Tag noindex/nofollow on every response, and the response body contains no internal identity fields (userId/sessionId/programId or snake_case equivalents).

loadCoachWeeklyWithClient() in src/lib/coach-weekly-data.ts builds a Supabase client from SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY that bypasses RLS, but every query is scoped by an explicit .eq("user_id", userId) predicate against the single hardcoded COACH_API_USER_ID passed in from the route, and it feeds the same shaped inputs into buildCoachCheckInReport(), loadStallAssessments(), and buildCoachRecommendations() rather than reimplementing aggregation.

Slice 0 of the in-app AI Coach shipped on 2026-09-20 and became multi-thread on 2026-09-27. It wraps Track Coach rather than replacing it, runs LangChain TypeScript in-process, and keeps the engine as the sole owner of numbers. Slices 1-5 remain specified and unbuilt. WRITE_TOOL_NAMES is empty, so drafts, confirm-chip startNextSession, and live mutations are not implemented.

Per docs/AI-COACH.md invariants, planned agent tools must take the user-scoped Supabase client from the request session and are never given SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY or COACH_API_TOKEN, keeping the agent's trust boundary separate from the weekly Coach API's elevated secret-client path; canonical figures must come only from sessionTarget(), buildCoachCheckInReport, buildCoachRecommendations, groupReviewSessions, and loadStallAssessments rather than being recomputed by the prompt.

A user may own many agent threads. The full transcript persists in owner-scoped agent_thread and agent_message rows, with parts stored as JSON so tool calls survive reload. selectModelMessages is the only cut: it sends the system prompt plus the last CONTEXT_MESSAGE_LIMIT of 20 messages, walking back so a tool row is not split from its call, then drops old tool results before user or assistant text once MODEL_CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET of 24000 characters is exceeded. Slices must still be built in order, and a later slice may add tools but must not weaken an earlier invariant.

GET /api/agent/chat never writes. It returns the latest 50 threads plus the latest thread, a draft for ?thread=new, the owned thread for a UUID, 404 for an unowned UUID, and 400 for any other thread query. Unauthenticated requests return 401.

POST /api/agent/chat requires an authenticated cookie session and a Gateway key before any write. A missing threadId key, blank text, or malformed id returns 400 with no writes. A missing AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN returns 503 with no writes. threadId null inserts a new thread, and an unowned threadId returns 404 with no agent run and no writes.

A successful chat turn streams SSE in a fixed order: thread with the saved summary and user message, then text, tool-start, and tool-end from the LangChain loop, then done with the persisted reply or error. startTurn inserts the thread only on the first send and deletes that row if the first message insert fails. Each saved message stamps agent_thread.updated_at to the message created_at.

The agent binds only four read tools on the request's user-scoped cookie client: weeklyCoach wraps loadCoachUi, activeProgram wraps getActiveProgram, exerciseReview uses the same finished-session grouping as exercise review, and nextWorkout hydrates targets through sessionTarget. These tools never receive SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY or COACH_API_TOKEN and do not recompute engine numbers.

One agent turn is capped at TOOL_CALL_BUDGET of 8 tool calls via toolCallLimitMiddleware with exitBehavior continue. The default model is openai/gpt-5.4 through the Vercel AI Gateway unless AGENT_MODEL overrides it. LangSmith traces are grouped by metadata.thread_id, which is the same app-chosen uuid7 stored as agent_thread.id. There is no checkpointer.

Agent chat chrome is a persistent Sheet entry on Lift, Track, Program, and You, hidden wherever hideAppChrome is true and omitted on /coach itself. /coach is the full-thread page. New chat is a client-side draft until the first send. The chatReducer adopts the thread event, and the page mirrors the open thread into ?thread= with replaceState. History, New chat, and Full screen are disabled while a turn streams.

Multi-thread ownership is enforced by RLS on each row's own user_id plus agent_message_thread_owner_fkey, a composite foreign key from (thread_id, user_id) to agent_thread (id, user_id) with on delete cascade. The 2026-09-27 migration deleted empty Slice 0 threads, backfilled titles, dropped the one-thread-per-user unique key, and removed the database default for agent_thread.id so the app must supply a uuid7.
